record.original_question: (M. Herzog, J. Schönheim). Let G be a group and let k ⩾ 2. Let H1,..., Hk be subgroups of G, and g1,..., gk elements of G such that the cosets g1 H1,..., gk Hk form a partition of G. Is it true that |G: Hi | = |G: Hj | for some i ̸= j? This is known to be true for groups with a Sylow tower(M. A. Berger, A. Felzenbaum, A. Fraenkel, Fund. Math., 128, no. 3(1987), 139–144). Also cf. 20.99.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $G$ be a group and let $k \geq 2$ be an integer. Suppose $H_1, \dots, H_k$ are subgroups of $G$ and $g_1, \dots, g_k$ are elements of $G$ such that the left cosets $g_1 H_1, \dots, g_k H_k$ form a partition of $G$ (that is, $G = \bigsqcup_{i=1}^{k} g_i H_i$ as a disjoint union). Prove or disprove: there must exist indices $i \neq j$ with $[G : H_i] = [G : H_j]$.
artifact.category_tag: Herzog–Schönheim conjecture / coset partitions of groups
artifact.status_search_result: The Herzog–Schönheim conjecture remains open in general. It is known for groups with a Sylow tower (Berger–Felzenbaum–Fraenkel, 1987), for finitely generated groups under additional hypotheses, for groups of order less than 1440, and most recently (2025) for simple groups and symmetric groups (Garonzi–Margolis), but the general case is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Herzog–Schönheim conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Herzog–Schönheim conjecture is a combinatorial problem in the area of group theory, posed by Marcel Herzog and Jochanan Schönheim in 1974.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is a longstanding open problem in group theory.

status_evidence.title: The Herzog-Schönheim conjecture for simple and symmetric groups
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the conjecture for simple and symmetric groups (2025).
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress establishes the conjecture for simple and symmetric groups, indicating the general case remains open.

status_evidence.title: The Herzog-Schonheim conjecture for finitely generated groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the conjecture in the finitely generated setting.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on partial cases, consistent with the general conjecture being open.
